subproblem.title: Diagonal extraction of one subsequence converging uniformly on countably many sets, with a single glued limit
subproblem.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers and L := L(R^n, R^l) with the operator norm. Let F_k : R^n -> L (k in N) be any maps and S_m (m in N) any subsets of R^n. Assume that for every m in N and every strictly increasing psi : N -> N there are a strictly increasing chi : N -> N and g : R^n -> L such that F_{psi(chi(j))} -> g uniformly on S_m as j -> infinity. Then there are a strictly increasing phi : N -> N and a single V : R^n -> L such that, for every m in N, F_{phi(j)} -> V uniformly on S_m as j -> infinity.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (F : ℕ → Rn n → (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ)) (S : ℕ → Set (Rn n)), (∀ (m : ℕ) (ψ : ℕ → ℕ), StrictMono ψ → ∃ (χ : ℕ → ℕ) (g : Rn n → (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ)), StrictMono χ ∧ TendstoUniformlyOn (fun j => F (ψ (χ j))) g atTop (S m)) → ∃ (φ : ℕ → ℕ) (V : Rn n → (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ)), StrictMono φ ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, TendstoUniformlyOn (fun j => F (φ j)) V atTop (S m)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 3-6 of the parent proof (diagonal construction, strict monotonicity, tails, glued limit), stated for arbitrary sets S_m in place of the balls B^m.
1. Choices. For every m in N and every map psi : N -> N choose a strictly increasing chi(m, psi) : N -> N and g(m, psi) : R^n -> L such that, whenever psi is strictly increasing, F_{psi(chi(m, psi)(j))} -> g(m, psi) uniformly on S_m as j -> infinity. For strictly increasing psi such a choice exists by hypothesis. For any other psi take chi(m, psi) := id and g(m, psi) := 0; the condition is then vacuous.
2. Nested subsequences. Define recursively (Nat.rec) Psi_0 := id and Psi_{m+1} := Psi_m o chi_m with chi_m := chi(m, Psi_m). By induction on m, every Psi_m is strictly increasing, as a composition of strictly increasing maps. Step 1 applies to the strictly increasing Psi_m and gives F_{Psi_{m+1}(j)} = F_{Psi_m(chi_m(j))} -> g_m := g(m, Psi_m) uniformly on S_m.
3. Later stages factor through earlier ones. For all m, d in N there is a strictly increasing rho_{m,d} : N -> N with Psi_{m+d} = Psi_m o rho_{m,d}. The proof is by induction on d. For d = 0 take rho_{m,0} := id. If Psi_{m+d} = Psi_m o rho_{m,d}, then Psi_{m+d+1} = Psi_{m+d} o chi_{m+d} = Psi_m o (rho_{m,d} o chi_{m+d}), and rho_{m,d+1} := rho_{m,d} o chi_{m+d} is strictly increasing.
4. The diagonal is strictly increasing. Put phi(j) := Psi_{j+1}(j). Every strictly increasing chi : N -> N satisfies chi(i) >= i for all i (induction on i; StrictMono.id_le). Hence chi_{j+1}(j+1) >= j+1 > j. Since Psi_{j+1} is strictly increasing, phi(j+1) = Psi_{j+2}(j+1) = Psi_{j+1}(chi_{j+1}(j+1)) > Psi_{j+1}(j) = phi(j). A map phi : N -> N with phi(j) < phi(j+1) for all j is strictly increasing (strictMono_nat_of_lt_succ).
5. Tails of phi are reindexings of Psi_{m+1}. Fix m and put tau_j := rho_{m+1, j-m}(j) for every j (truncated subtraction).
 a. For j >= m we have j + 1 = (m+1) + (j-m). By step 3, phi(j) = Psi_{j+1}(j) = Psi_{m+1}(rho_{m+1,j-m}(j)) = Psi_{m+1}(tau_j).
 b. Since rho_{m+1,j-m} is strictly increasing, tau_j >= j for every j, so tau_j -> infinity.
 c. Uniform convergence survives reindexing by a sequence tending to infinity. Given epsilon > 0, step 2 gives I with ||F_{Psi_{m+1}(i)}(z) - g_m(z)|| < epsilon for all i >= I and z in S_m. Moreover tau_j >= I for all j >= I. So F_{Psi_{m+1}(tau_j)} -> g_m uniformly on S_m (in Lean: for each entourage u, apply Tendsto.eventually of tau_j -> infinity to the eventual statement for u).
 d. F_{phi(j)} = F_{Psi_{m+1}(tau_j)} for all j >= m, and changing finitely many terms does not affect uniform convergence (TendstoUniformlyOn.congr with an eventual EqOn). Hence F_{phi(j)} -> g_m uniformly on S_m.
6. Gluing.
 a. Define V(z) := g_{m(z)}(z), where m(z) is the least m with z in S_m (Nat.find) if some S_m contains z, and V(z) := 0 otherwise.
 b. Let m in N and z in S_m. Then m(z) exists and z lies in S_{m(z)}. Evaluating step 5 at z gives F_{phi(j)}(z) -> g_m(z) and F_{phi(j)}(z) -> g_{m(z)}(z). Limits in the Hausdorff space L are unique (TendstoUniformlyOn.tendsto_at, tendsto_nhds_unique), so g_m(z) = g_{m(z)}(z) = V(z).
 c. Thus V = g_m on S_m. Replacing the limit by a function that agrees with it on S_m preserves uniform convergence on S_m (TendstoUniformlyOn.congr_right). Hence F_{phi(j)} -> V uniformly on S_m for every m. QED.
proof_key_steps: choose chi(m, psi) and g(m, psi) for every psi; the convergence condition is required only for strictly increasing psi
Psi_0 = id and Psi_{m+1} = Psi_m o chi(m, Psi_m) are strictly increasing, and F o Psi_{m+1} -> g_m uniformly on S_m
Psi_{m+d} = Psi_m o rho_{m,d} with rho_{m,d} strictly increasing
phi(j) = Psi_{j+1}(j) is strictly increasing because chi(i) >= i for strictly increasing chi
for j >= m, phi(j) = Psi_{m+1}(tau_j) with tau_j >= j, so F o phi -> g_m uniformly on S_m
V(z) := g_{least m with z in S_m}(z); uniqueness of limits gives V = g_m on S_m

audit.reason: The one-line proposition exactly matches the prose, including arbitrary sets without nesting or covering assumptions. The recursive extractions give a strictly increasing diagonal; each fixed tail factors through its convergent subsequence with indices at least j. Uniqueness of limits validates gluing on overlaps, and zero defines the complement. The proof is complete and independent of the parent.

subproblem.title: Hoelder bounds pass to pointwise limits, and the limit is continuous
subproblem.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, L := L(R^n, R^l) with the operator norm, alpha > 0 and K >= 0 real, F_j : R^n -> L (j in N) and V : R^n -> L with F_j(z) -> V(z) for every z in R^n. Assume that for all z, z' in R^n, ||F_j(z) - F_j(z')|| <= K |z - z'|^alpha for all sufficiently large j. Then ||V(z) - V(z')|| <= K |z - z'|^alpha for all z, z' in R^n, and V is continuous.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (α K : ℝ) (F : ℕ → Rn n → (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ)) (V : Rn n → (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ)), 0 < α → 0 ≤ K → (∀ z, Tendsto (fun j => F j z) atTop (𝓝 (V z))) → (∀ z z' : Rn n, ∀ᶠ j in atTop, ‖F j z - F j z'‖ ≤ K * ‖z - z'‖ ^ α) → (∀ z z' : Rn n, ‖V z - V z'‖ ≤ K * ‖z - z'‖ ^ α) ∧ Continuous V
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 7b-c of the parent proof, stated for a general pointwise convergent sequence.
1. Hoelder bound. Fix z, z' in R^n. By pointwise convergence, F_j(z) - F_j(z') -> V(z) - V(z'). By continuity of the norm, ||F_j(z) - F_j(z')|| -> ||V(z) - V(z')|| (Tendsto.sub, Tendsto.norm). By hypothesis these real numbers are at most c := K |z - z'|^alpha for all large j. The interval (-infinity, c] is closed, so the limit also satisfies ||V(z) - V(z')|| <= K |z - z'|^alpha (le_of_tendsto).
2. Continuity. Fix z.
 a. The map t -> K t^alpha is continuous at t = 0, because alpha > 0 (Real.continuousAt_rpow_const 0 alpha, using 0 <= alpha), and its value there is K * 0^alpha = 0 (Real.zero_rpow). The map z' -> |z' - z| is continuous with value 0 at z' = z. So K |z' - z|^alpha -> 0 as z' -> z.
 b. By step 1, 0 <= ||V(z') - V(z)|| <= K |z' - z|^alpha for every z'. By the squeeze theorem (squeeze_zero), ||V(z') - V(z)|| -> 0, that is, V(z') -> V(z) as z' -> z (tendsto_iff_norm_sub_tendsto_zero).
 c. So V is continuous at every point, hence continuous (continuous_iff_continuousAt). QED.
proof_key_steps: ||F_j(z) - F_j(z')|| -> ||V(z) - V(z')|| and is eventually <= K|z - z'|^alpha, so the limit obeys the same bound
K|z' - z|^alpha -> 0 as z' -> z because alpha > 0
the squeeze theorem gives continuity of V at every point

audit.reason: The exact type correctly permits the eventual threshold to depend on the pair of points. Pointwise convergence, continuous subtraction and norm, and closedness of the real order bound establish the global Holder estimate. Positivity of alpha makes the comparison function vanish at zero; squeezing proves continuity everywhere. The supplied proof is complete and has no child or parent dependencies.

subproblem.title: Uniformly Hoelder sequences converging on a dense subset of a compact set converge uniformly
subproblem.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, L := L(R^n, R^l) with the operator norm, alpha > 0 and K >= 0 real, S a compact subset of R^n, and D a subset of S whose closure contains S. Let F_j : R^n -> L (j in N) satisfy ||F_j(z) - F_j(z')|| <= K |z - z'|^alpha for every j and all z, z' in S. Assume that for every d in D the sequence (F_j(d))_j converges in L. Then there is G : R^n -> L with F_j -> G uniformly on S as j -> infinity.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (α K : ℝ) (S D : Set (Rn n)) (F : ℕ → Rn n → (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ)), 0 < α → 0 ≤ K → IsCompact S → D ⊆ S → S ⊆ closure D → (∀ d ∈ D, ∃ v : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ, Tendsto (fun j => F j d) atTop (𝓝 v)) → (∀ j, ∀ z ∈ S, ∀ z' ∈ S, ‖F j z - F j z'‖ ≤ K * ‖z - z'‖ ^ α) → ∃ G : Rn n → (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ), TendstoUniformlyOn F G atTop S
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 2d-e of the parent proof. That step cites the Arzela-Ascoli theorem BoundedContinuousFunction.arzela_ascoli. Its module Mathlib.Topology.ContinuousMap.Bounded.ArzelaAscoli is not imported by the frozen contract, so the classical proof is supplied here: the uniform Hoelder bound (equicontinuity) upgrades convergence on a dense subset of a compact set to uniform convergence.
1. Limits on D. For d in D let v(d) be the limit of F_j(d).
2. A Hoelder scale. Let epsilon > 0. The function t -> K t^alpha is continuous at t = 0, because alpha > 0, and its value there is K * 0^alpha = 0. (Real.continuousAt_rpow_const 0 alpha, using 0 <= alpha, and Real.zero_rpow.) So there is delta > 0 with K t^alpha < epsilon/3 whenever |t| < delta (Metric.eventually_nhds_iff). Put eta := delta/2 > 0; only this positive value t = eta is used below. Then K eta^alpha < epsilon/3.
3. A finite net inside D. Let z in S. Since z lies in the closure of D, there is d in D with |z - d| < eta. Hence the open balls B_eta(d), d in D, cover S. S is compact, so finitely many of them cover S (IsCompact.elim_finite_subcover_image; Metric.mem_closure_iff for the cover): there is a finite subset T of D with S contained in the union of the balls B_eta(d), d in T.
4. Cauchy at the net points. T is finite and F_j(d) -> v(d) for every d in T. So there is N with ||F_j(d) - v(d)|| < epsilon/6 for all j >= N and all d in T (Set.Finite.eventually_all, then eventually_atTop). Then ||F_j(d) - F_{j'}(d)|| <= ||F_j(d) - v(d)|| + ||F_{j'}(d) - v(d)|| < epsilon/3 for all j, j' >= N and d in T.
5. Uniform Cauchy estimate. Let j, j' >= N and z in S. Pick d in T with |z - d| < eta. Since d lies in D, a subset of S, the Hoelder hypothesis applies to z and d: ||F_j(z) - F_j(d)|| <= K |z - d|^alpha <= K eta^alpha < epsilon/3. This uses that t -> t^alpha is monotone on [0, infinity) and that K >= 0. Likewise ||F_{j'}(d) - F_{j'}(z)|| < epsilon/3. By the triangle inequality, ||F_j(z) - F_{j'}(z)|| < epsilon/3 + epsilon/3 + epsilon/3 = epsilon. So (F_j) is uniformly Cauchy on S (Metric.uniformCauchySeqOn_iff).
6. The limit function. For z in S the sequence (F_j(z)) is Cauchy in L. L is complete, being a finite-dimensional normed space, so the sequence converges (UniformCauchySeqOn.cauchySeq, cauchySeq_tendsto_of_complete, tendsto_nhds_limUnder). Let G(z) be the limit of F_j(z) whenever it exists (for instance limUnder atTop), and arbitrary otherwise. Then F_j(z) -> G(z) for every z in S.
7. Uniform convergence. Let epsilon > 0 and take N as in step 5. For j >= N and z in S we have ||F_j(z) - F_{j'}(z)|| < epsilon for every j' >= N. Letting j' -> infinity gives ||F_j(z) - G(z)|| <= epsilon. This holds for all j >= N and all z in S, so F_j -> G uniformly on S (in Mathlib: UniformCauchySeqOn.tendstoUniformlyOn_of_tendsto). QED.
proof_key_steps: choose eta > 0 with K eta^alpha < epsilon/3, using continuity of t -> K t^alpha at 0
by compactness, finitely many balls B_eta(d) with centres d in a finite subset T of D cover S
the finitely many convergent sequences F_j(d), d in T, are simultaneously epsilon/3-Cauchy from some N on
the triangle inequality and the Hoelder bound give the uniform Cauchy estimate on S
L is complete, so a pointwise limit G exists on S; uniformly Cauchy plus pointwise convergence gives uniform convergence

audit.reason: All hypotheses appear in the exact standalone type. The positive Holder scale, finite net inside D, and simultaneous Cauchy estimates establish uniform Cauchyness. Completeness supplies pointwise limits, and the cited uniform-Cauchy lemma gives uniform convergence. The final non-strict epsilon estimate suffices by epsilon rescaling. Empty S and K = 0 cause no gap.

subproblem.title: Sequential Arzela-Ascoli for uniformly bounded, uniformly Hoelder maps on a compact set
subproblem.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, L := L(R^n, R^l) with the operator norm, alpha > 0, K >= 0 and M real, and S a compact subset of R^n. Let g_j : R^n -> L (j in N) satisfy ||g_j(z)|| <= M for every j and z in S, and ||g_j(z) - g_j(z')|| <= K |z - z'|^alpha for every j and all z, z' in S. Then there are a strictly increasing chi : N -> N and G : R^n -> L with g_{chi(j)} -> G uniformly on S as j -> infinity.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (α K M : ℝ) (S : Set (Rn n)) (g : ℕ → Rn n → (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ)), 0 < α → 0 ≤ K → IsCompact S → (∀ j, ∀ z ∈ S, ‖g j z‖ ≤ M) → (∀ j, ∀ z ∈ S, ∀ z' ∈ S, ‖g j z - g j z'‖ ≤ K * ‖z - z'‖ ^ α) → ∃ (χ : ℕ → ℕ) (G : Rn n → (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ)), StrictMono χ ∧ TendstoUniformlyOn (fun j => g (χ j)) G atTop S
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 2b-e of the parent proof (Arzela-Ascoli on a compact set). The theorem cited there, BoundedContinuousFunction.arzela_ascoli, is not imported by the frozen contract. It is replaced by its classical proof through the sibling lemmas diagonal_extract (Submission.dohr_eb_sch_bu_hds_diagonal_extract) and unif_of_dense (Submission.dohr_eb_sch_bu_hds_unif_of_dense).
1. Empty case. If S is empty, take chi := id and G := 0. Uniform convergence on the empty set holds trivially (tendstoUniformlyOn_empty).
2. A countable dense subset. Assume S is nonempty. R^n is second countable, hence so is the subspace S, which is therefore separable. So there is a countable set D with D contained in S and S contained in the closure of D (TopologicalSpace.exists_countable_dense_subset). D is nonempty, because S is nonempty and the closure of the empty set is empty. A nonempty countable set is the range of a sequence (Set.Countable.exists_eq_range), so D = {d_m : m in N} for some d : N -> R^n.
3. Extraction at one point. Let m in N and let psi : N -> N be strictly increasing. Since d_m lies in D, a subset of S, ||g_{psi(j)}(d_m)|| <= M for every j. So the sequence j -> g_{psi(j)}(d_m) lies in the closed ball of radius M about 0 in L. That ball is compact (isCompact_closedBall), because L is a finite-dimensional normed space and hence proper. L is a metric space, so a sequence in a compact set has a convergent subsequence (IsCompact.tendsto_subseq). Thus there are a strictly increasing chi and v in L with g_{psi(chi(j))}(d_m) -> v. Uniform convergence on a singleton is convergence at its point (tendstoUniformlyOn_singleton_iff_tendsto), so g_{psi(chi(j))} -> (the constant map with value v) uniformly on {d_m}.
4. Diagonal over the points of D. Step 3 is exactly the hypothesis of diagonal_extract for F := g and S_m := {d_m}. That lemma gives a strictly increasing chi : N -> N and W : R^n -> L with g_{chi(j)} -> W uniformly on {d_m} for every m. Hence, for every d in D, writing d = d_m, the sequence g_{chi(j)}(d) converges to W(d_m) (TendstoUniformlyOn.tendsto_at).
5. Upgrade to uniform convergence. Apply unif_of_dense to F_j := g_{chi(j)}, the compact set S and the set D, which is contained in S and whose closure contains S. Its Hoelder hypothesis holds because every g_k is K-alpha-Hoelder on S, and its convergence hypothesis on D holds by step 4. It gives G : R^n -> L with g_{chi(j)} -> G uniformly on S. Together with the strictly increasing chi of step 4 this is the claim. QED.
proof_key_steps: if S is empty the claim is trivial
take a countable dense subset D of S and enumerate it as (d_m)
at each d_m every subsequence has a further convergent subsequence, by compactness of the closed M-ball in the finite-dimensional L
diagonal_extract with S_m = {d_m} gives chi with g_{chi(j)} convergent at every point of D
unif_of_dense upgrades convergence on D to uniform convergence on S

audit.reason: The type matches the prose, including unrestricted real M. The proof handles empty S, enumerates a nonempty countable dense subset otherwise, and extracts at each point using compactness of the operator-norm M-ball. Applying diagonal_extract to singletons and then unif_of_dense proves the conclusion. These are exactly its declared dependencies, with no circular use of compact extraction or the parent.
